segments.text: A pilot ejects fourteen kilometres up, falls into a thunderstorm, and the storm throws him back up.
No chance. Storms don't hold on to people. Let's go look.
July {1959|nineteen fifty-nine}. Marine pilot William Rankin flies over a thunderhead when his engine dies. The emergency power handle snaps off in his hand.
He ejects with no pressure suit, into air fifty below zero. Frostbite. His belly swells.
His parachute opens inside the storm. Updrafts hurl him back up. Hail. Blue sheets of lightning. Rain so thick he holds his breath.
It should take minutes. The storm keeps him for forty.
Then it drops him into trees in North Carolina.
He walks to a road, gets a ride, and flies again. I was wrong. Case closed.
